code.displayName: Follow-up encounter
code.originalText: Diagnosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma: tumor board plan, medical oncology consultation, genetic counseling, early palliative care, and planning of chemotherapy before surgery

code.displayName: Reason for referral (narrative)

text.paragraph: Suspected pancreatic or duodenal cancer in a 32-year-old playwright with two months of epigastric pain boring through to the back, a 5 kg weight loss, black stools with iron deficiency anemia (hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, ferritin 6 ng/mL), new diabetes (A1c 6.6%) and a cholestatic liver pattern. Upper endoscopy and pancreas-protocol CT are booked this week. Please see her within two weeks to review the results with her and plan treatment if cancer is found. [S]

list.item: What is the diagnosis and its stage, and what further tests are needed to decide whether it can be removed?
What treatment do you recommend, in what order (chemotherapy, surgery, or both), and what is its aim?
Which genetic tests should be done, on her blood and on the tumor, and what would the results mean for her and her family?
How should her pain, nutrition, digestion, new diabetes and anemia be managed during treatment, and when should palliative care start?
What is her risk of blood clots, and what should be done about it given the bleeding?
What should she know about fertility and contraception, and what monitoring should primary care share?

code.displayName: History of Present illness Narrative

text.paragraph: Ms. Hansberry, 32, is seen at the request of Dr. Marchetti-Fields two weeks after she presented with two months of epigastric and back pain, weight loss, black stools with iron deficiency anemia, and new diabetes. Since then she has had an upper endoscopy, a pancreas-protocol CT, an endoscopic ultrasound with biopsy and a biliary stent, two doses of intravenous iron, and review at our pancreatic tumor board. The pain is 6 out of 10 and breaks her sleep; her stools are pale and float after fatty meals; there has been no black stool since the iron. She works at home as a playwright and is active most of the day (ECOG 1). She is not pregnant and has no children. She asked for the facts in plain words. [S]
Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Lorraine Vivian Hansberry was born in Chicago on May 19, 1930, the youngest of four children of Carl Augustus Hansberry, a successful real estate broker who founded one of the city's first Black banks, and Nannie Louise (Perry) Hansberry, a schoolteacher. Her grandfather had been born enslaved. [D]

In 1937 her family moved into a house in the all-white Washington Park subdivision of Woodlawn in defiance of a racially restrictive covenant. The resulting case, Hansberry v. Lee, was decided in the family's favor by the U.S. Supreme Court in 1940. [D]
Her father died suddenly in Mexico in 1946 of a cerebral hemorrhage while planning to move the family there. [D]

She enrolled at the University of Wisconsin in 1948, left in 1950 for New York, and wrote for the newspaper Freedom. In June 1953 she married Robert Nemiroff. Sources differ on when they divorced (1962 or 1964); they continued to work together. [D]

A Raisin in the Sun opened at the Ethel Barrymore Theatre on Broadway on March 11, 1959, the first play by a Black woman to be produced on Broadway. It won the New York Drama Critics' Circle Award; she was the first Black playwright and, at 29, the youngest American to win it. In 1962 she moved to Croton-on-Hudson, New York. [D]
One account dates the start of her illness to April 1963, when she began to suffer from fainting spells and attacks of nausea; tests pointed at first to what was suspected to be a duodenal ulcer. [D]

text.paragraph: 5 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.

Evaluation note

list.item: Adenocarcinoma of the head of the pancreas, borderline resectable (C25.0). Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma of the head of the pancreas invading the duodenum, which explains the bleeding, the anemia, the obstructed bile and pancreatic ducts, the pain and the new diabetes. By NCCN criteria it is borderline resectable, because the tumor contacts more than half the circumference of the superior mesenteric vein, although the vein can be reconstructed and no artery is involved; there is no distant spread on CT. For borderline resectable disease, chemotherapy first is preferred over going straight to surgery: it treats cancer that may already have spread unseen, can shrink the tumor away from the vein, and shows whether the cancer is controlled before a major operation. She is young and fit, with normal kidney function and bilirubin now normal, so modified FOLFIRINOX is the regimen of choice. The aim is cure, and surgery after chemotherapy offers the best chance of it; she was also told honestly that pancreatic cancer often returns even after successful surgery. [S]

Diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer (E08.9). New diabetes with weight loss at her age is caused by the cancer (type 3c), not type 2. It may worsen after removal of the head of the pancreas, and insulin is the treatment if glucose-lowering is needed; dexamethasone should be limited. [S]

Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (K86.81). Pale floating stools and weight loss with a blocked pancreatic duct: start enzyme replacement now on clinical grounds, without waiting for a stool test. [S]
Cancer-related pain (G89.3). Moderate tumor pain; low-dose opioid with a bowel regimen first, and EUS-guided celiac plexus neurolysis if it becomes severe. [S]

text.paragraph: Data reviewed: Dr. Marchetti-Fields's intake note and results. Upper endoscopy: an ulcerated, oozing mass on the medial wall of the second part of the duodenum beside the papilla, no peptic ulcer; biopsies: adenocarcinoma infiltrating from the pancreas. Pancreas-protocol CT with CT of the chest: 3.1 cm hypoattenuating mass in the pancreatic head invading the duodenum; common bile duct 13 mm and pancreatic duct 5 mm; contact with about 200 degrees of the superior mesenteric vein with short-segment narrowing that can be reconstructed; no contact with the superior mesenteric artery, celiac axis or common hepatic artery; no liver, peritoneal or lung lesion. EUS-guided biopsy: pancreatic adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated; extra cores held for molecular profiling. ERCP: fully covered metal stent across a distal bile duct stricture. Today: bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 168 U/L, CA 19-9 486 U/mL (after drainage), CEA 3.9 ng/mL, hemoglobin 10.4 g/dL, neutrophils 4.6, platelets 366, creatinine 0.68 mg/dL, albumin 3.5 g/dL, fasting glucose 141 mg/dL, INR 1.0. [S]

code.displayName: Plan of care note

list.item: Modified FOLFIRINOX every two weeks for six cycles (about three months) before surgery, through a port: oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, irinotecan 150 mg/m2, leucovorin 400 mg/m2 and fluorouracil 2400 mg/m2 over 46 hours, with pegfilgrastim on day 3; dose reductions for toxicity rather than delays where possible. [S]

Restaging with CA 19-9 every two cycles and pancreas-protocol CT after four and after six cycles; tumor board review after restaging, and pancreaticoduodenectomy with vein resection if there is no progression. [S]
Chemotherapy after surgery to complete about six months of treatment in all, the regimen chosen by her tolerance and the pathology. [S]

Germline multigene panel after genetic counseling, as for every patient with pancreatic cancer, and tumor molecular profiling on the EUS cores; cascade testing for blood relatives only if a germline variant is found. [S]
Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV screening and a pregnancy test before cycle 1; PCV20 and recombinant zoster vaccine now, before chemotherapy; no live vaccines. [S]

Antiemetic prevention with fosaprepitant, palonosetron, one day of dexamethasone and olanzapine on days 1 to 4, sparing further dexamethasone because of her diabetes; loperamide teaching for irinotecan diarrhea; neuropathy checks before each oxaliplatin dose. [S]
Palliative care from now, alongside cancer treatment; oxycodone 5 mg as needed with senna; pancrelipase about 72,000 lipase units with meals and half that with snacks; dietitian review. [S]
Home glucose monitoring, no glucose-lowering drug for now, insulin after surgery if needed; dilated eye examination and urine albumin at diagnosis of diabetes. [S]
Khorana score 3: prophylactic apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily once the duodenal bleeding has settled for several weeks; enoxaparin for four weeks after surgery. [S]
Fertility counseling before chemotherapy; effective non-estrogen contraception during treatment. [S]
Primary care to share the monitoring: blood counts and glucose at visits, mood and distress screening, weight, and help with symptoms between oncology visits. [S]

Discussed with Dr. Marchetti-Fields the same day and presented at the pancreatic tumor board with surgery, radiology and pathology. The images and biopsy results were explained to Ms. Hansberry in plain words, with the aim of treatment and its uncertainty; she chose to start chemotherapy without delaying for fertility preservation. She decides who else receives this note. [S]

Follow-up: Port placement next week; cycle 1 in two weeks; oncology review before each cycle; restaging after cycles 4 and 6; Dr. Marchetti-Fields continues primary care and shares the monitoring. [S]
